what_its_for: Tazarotene is a vitamin A-based cream, gel, or foam used to treat acne, plaque psoriasis (a skin condition that causes red, scaly patches), and to reduce the appearance of fine wrinkles, dark spots, and rough skin on the face.
how_to_take: Wash and dry your skin gently before applying. Apply a thin layer of tazarotene to the affected area(s) once daily, usually in the evening or at bedtime. Use only enough to cover the area — a little goes a long way. Wash your hands thoroughly after applying. Do not get it in your eyes, mouth, or nostrils. If it accidentally gets in your eyes, rinse well with water right away. For psoriasis, avoid applying to skin folds or areas where skin rubs together unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: Use tazarotene once a day in the evening, exactly as your doctor prescribed. The strength and form (cream, gel, or foam) will depend on your condition. Do not use more than directed — using too much can cause more irritation without better results.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and apply your next dose at your regular time the following evening. Do not apply a double dose to make up for the missed one.
storage: Store tazarotene at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat and open flames — the foam form is flammable. Keep the cap tightly closed and keep it out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting tazarotene on unaffected skin, in your eyes, mouth, or nose. Avoid using harsh soaps, scrubs, or other skin products that are drying or irritating (like products containing alcohol, spices, or lime) on treated areas. Avoid waxing or using hair removal products on treated skin. Avoid sunlamps and tanning beds. Limit time in the sun and always wear sunscreen (SPF 30 or higher) and protective clothing when outdoors, as tazarotene makes your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Do not use if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — tazarotene can harm an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you experience severe skin redness, peeling, burning, or blistering that does not improve. Also call if you develop a skin rash or hives, have signs of an allergic reaction (swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing), notice excessive dryness or skin discoloration, or if your condition is getting worse instead of better. Women of childbearing age should contact their doctor right away if they become pregnant while using this medication.
when_it_works: For acne, you may start to see improvement in 4 to 8 weeks, but it can take up to 12 weeks (about 3 months) for the full benefit. For psoriasis, improvement is often seen within 1 to 4 weeks. For fine lines and dark spots, results may take several months of consistent use. Mild irritation, redness, or peeling in the first few weeks is normal as your skin adjusts — this usually improves with continued use.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT use tazarotene if you are pregnant or trying to become pregnant. It can cause serious birth defects. Use effective birth control while using this medication. Take a pregnancy test before starting if there is any chance you could be pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if tazarotene passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using it if you are breastfeeding. Children: The safety of tazarotene in children under 12 years old has not been established. For acne, it is approved for patients 12 years and older. Older adults: Older adults may be more sensitive to skin irritation from tazarotene. Use with caution and as directed by your doctor.
